_readme: STARLINK HARDWARE — what we have verified, and when.
Every figure here is operator-approved and DATED. Starlink changes hardware
generations, so a specification is not permanent truth: it is what was true on
verified_on, according to source. Past stale_after_days the AI stops stating
these confidently and offers to confirm instead — that is the whole point of
the date being a required field rather than a comment.
null means WE DO NOT KNOW. It is never rendered as unlimited, standard, none,
or any other value. Leave a field null rather than guessing it.
NO PRICES. Hardware prices live in uCRM and nowhere else; a test fails if a
price appears in this file. Specs here, money there, always.
Ethernet is per-model on purpose. Answering 'does Starlink have Ethernet'
generically is the single clearest mark of a chatbot that does not know the
product — the answer differs by generation, so the model must be established

models.summary: Compact Starlink hardware for basic internet, fixed or portable.
models.wifi: Wi-Fi is built into the dish — no separate router. WiFi 5 (802.11a/b/g/n/ac), dual band 3x3 MU-MIMO, WPA2. Works with Starlink mesh.
models.ethernet: One latching Ethernet LAN port, used with the Starlink Plug that comes in the box. No separate adapter is needed for it.
models.environment: IP67 Type 4 with the DC power cable and Starlink Plug fitted; -30C to +50C; operational in wind of 96 kph and above; melts snow up to 25 mm/hour
best_for: sites running on solar or a small battery
anywhere the kit has to move
limitations: Built-in Wi-Fi only — a larger building needs access points added.
Not the starting point for an office, hotel, factory or school.
models.source: Starlink Mini / Standard specification sheets, supplied by DishNet
models.in_the_box: dish with integrated WiFi, kickstand, pipe adapter and flat mount, 15 m DC power cable, power supply, Starlink Plug

models.summary: The normal fixed installation for higher-demand everyday use.
models.wifi: Ships with Router 3: WiFi 6 (802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax), tri band 4x4 MU-MIMO, WPA2. Meshes only with Starlink Gen 2 and Router 3 nodes, up to 3 — NOT with third-party mesh systems.
models.ethernet: Router 3, which ships with current Standard, has TWO latching Ethernet LAN ports under a removable cover. Older Standard generations differ — establish which kit the customer has before answering.
models.environment: Dish IP67 Type 4, -30C to +50C, operational in wind of 96 kph and above, melts snow up to 40 mm/hour. Router 3 is IP56 and is for indoor use.
best_for: a fixed installation that will not move
the usual starting point for a small office
limitations: Physically larger and needs a proper fixed mount.
Draws noticeably more power than Mini — matters on solar.
Router coverage is not building-wide Wi-Fi on its own.
Router 3 does not mesh with third-party systems — only Starlink nodes.
models.source: Starlink Mini / Standard specification sheets, supplied by DishNet
models.in_the_box: dish, kickstand, Router 3, cables and power supply

models.summary: For demanding sites and harder environments, where it is offered and appropriate.
models.power_avg_w: significantly more than Standard — confirm the current figure before advising on solar
limitations: Never recommend it just because it costs more — establish the requirement first.
A five-person household almost never needs it.
Several specifications here are not yet verified: say so and confirm.
